summary: Upgrade Psycopg to avoid PGlite timestamp loader crashes

delivery.outcome: Keep the PGlite-backed gateway alive when timestamp results are read by the pinned binary Psycopg driver.
nonGoals: No application, DB adapter, protocol or schema changes
No claim that the full upstream native root cause is proven
Preserve the separately owned runtime-copy ticket-036

architecture.decision: Upgrade the existing Psycopg/binary pin from 3.3.6 to 3.3.9. A controlled image comparison reproduces SIGSEGV for timestamp results with 3.3.6 and succeeds with 3.3.9 against the same PGlite server, SQL, threading and gRPC probe; integer-only results are a positive control.
architecture.rollback: Restore the previous dependency pin through an independently reviewed change; retain the failing native reproduction.

runtimeDependencies: psycopg[binary]==3.3.9 (patch update of an existing dependency)

validation.evidence: Old timestamp query exits 139; integer-only control and new timestamp query exit 0 on the same PGlite data and runtime base.
Installed versions match the candidate pin; live PGlite gateway, all transports, persistence, logs and MCP pass without adapter changes or weakened checks.

commands: protected exact-head Validator review and merge
validation.evidence: Required CI and trusted App approval bind the final head; main CI and owner cleanup are recorded externally.
